decisions.reason: The assigned Definition specifies only the total raw comparison y(Phi_h)>c_h. It does not assert all-input agreement with a posterior marginal mode. In the proposed scalar field, Phi_h=1, c_h=0 and the raw output is indeed 0 while the basis-defined posterior mode is 2. This is allowed: thm-ip-isonormal-gaussian-posterior-law states the feature-mean identity only P_Y-almost surely for fixed h, and thm-ip-map-test-level-and-power Statement and step 1.3 use precisely that qualification. Under P_Y, Y(1)=2Y(1/2) almost surely, so the displayed witness is an exceptional input, not a contradiction. The resolvent exists since epsilon>0; both comparison branches cover every real field evaluation. No item change is warranted.

The repository defines N to contain 0 (def-natural-numbers Definition). The assigned Example instead gives Kx and h only on j>=1, so neither is specified as an element of the declared l2(N), and the asserted basis omits e_0. This is a well-definedness defect in the example interface, rather than a failed range argument or a missing citation. Repaired by explicitly setting I={j in N:j>=1} and using l2(I,R) throughout the Example. The bijective isometric reindexing x -> (x_(n+1)) transfers the existing completeness supplier; tail sums prove basis density. The original compactness and non-estimability conclusions are retained. Also corrected the inherited Countable Choice accounting without strengthening its assumed axiom.
